agree.reason: The evidence makes a reasonable case, but nothing gives an editor with a $9,000 budget and an $8,000 alternative a reason to go above budget, such as committed dates or the free extras, so she may well counter or pass.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the unsupported claim that every other publisher pays $12,000 and invents no numbers, though 'my rate elsewhere has gone up' rests on a single $12,500 book.

works_the_facts.reason: It lists the raw facts but works out nothing from them: not the per-month earnings on a four-month job, not how far $11,500 sits below $12,500 or inside the agent's range, and not the fourth printing.

right_comparison.reason: It compares against another publisher's fee but never takes on the editor's real alternative: a newer illustrator with no bestselling or reading-list record, at $8,000.

qualification.reason: The email has no hedges and the ask doesn't need one; the missing delivery commitments are scored under objections.

objections.reason: The budget objection and the cheaper-illustrator option are left unanswered, and the available offsets (sketches within 6 weeks, final art by September 1, two free spot drawings) go unused.

fit.reason: It is a well-toned email under 250 words, but it keeps placeholders even though the names and title (Nadia, Elena, The Night Garden) were known, and it neither makes the requested 'everyone pays more' point in an honest form nor explains why it was left out.
